narrativeReportMd:
# Substance R4-to-R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
`Substance` remains the same canonical resource in R6, but there are material local breaking changes. The highest-impact changes are the mandatory `Substance.code` representation change from `CodeableConcept` to `CodeableReference(SubstanceDefinition)`, removal of the repeatable `Substance.instance` backbone, and removal of the repeatable `Substance.ingredient` backbone.

## Scope
The analysis is limited to the `Substance` StructureDefinition and directly related local terminology and datatype/resource definitions. Inherited base-resource changes are excluded from `findings[]` and listed as out of scope.

## Main migration themes
R6 makes `Substance` a lighter resource: substance identity now points to `SubstanceDefinition` through `CodeableReference`, package/container details are flattened to top-level optional fields, and composition/ingredient details no longer live inside `Substance`. R4 instances with nested `instance` or `ingredient` content will need structural transforms, and some transforms are not lossless without external policy.

## Highest-impact findings
The mandatory `code` element changes wire shape and allows references to `SubstanceDefinition`; existing R4 JSON using a direct `CodeableConcept` at `Substance.code` is not valid R6. R4 `instance` and `ingredient` elements are absent in R6, so instances carrying package/container or composition data become invalid unless transformed.

## Findings requiring human review
Human review is most important for mapping multiple R4 package/container instances, preserving the distinction between substance identifiers and container identifiers, and deciding whether R4 ingredient data belongs in R6 `Ingredient`, `SubstanceDefinition.relationship`, another artifact, or an extension.

## Backward-compatible design observations
Several changes appear aligned with the newer R6 `SubstanceDefinition` and `Ingredient` model, but they could have been less disruptive if R4 backbones or a separate optional reference field had been retained and deprecated through profiles or guidance.

## Follow-up analysis
Review the assigned reports for `SubstanceDefinition`, `Ingredient`, `CodeableReference`, and relevant terminology/search artifacts before finalizing a cross-version migration plan.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: `Substance` has high-impact local breaking changes: `code` has a new `CodeableReference` representation, `instance` was removed/flattened, and `ingredient` was removed. The main uncertainty is the intended official migration path for package/container and ingredient data.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Migration is not just a field rename. Systems must adopt the R6 `CodeableReference` wire shape, decide how to create or reference `SubstanceDefinition`, flatten at most one set of package/container details into top-level `expiry` and `quantity`, and move composition data out of `Substance`. Lossless migration is doubtful for repeated R4 `instance` entries or ingredient records without additional business rules.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for the computable StructureDefinition deltas because the R4 and R6 local differentials and snapshots agree. Confidence is lower for intended semantic mappings because official narrative diffs, ConceptMaps, and terminology expansions were not supplied.

findings.title: Substance.code changed from CodeableConcept to CodeableReference(SubstanceDefinition)

binding.description: Codes defining the type of substance.

semanticText.definition: A code (or set of codes) that identify this substance.

oldState.narrativeMd: In R4, the required substance identity was carried directly as a `CodeableConcept` at `Substance.code`, with codings/text directly under the `code` element.

newState.summary: `Substance.code` is a mandatory `CodeableReference` that can contain a concept or a reference to `SubstanceDefinition`.

binding.description: Codes defining the type of substance.

semanticText.definition: A code (or set of codes) that identify this substance.

newState.narrativeMd: In R6, codings must be nested under `Substance.code.concept`, or the element may instead carry `Substance.code.reference` to a `SubstanceDefinition` resource.

facts.note: The element name is unchanged, but the JSON/XML child structure is different.
The field remains mandatory, so every valid instance is exposed to the type replacement.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The same element id and path are present in both versions; only the declared type domain changed.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is a direct representation break for strict validators and generated models. A valid R4 instance with `code.coding` directly under `Substance.code` does not satisfy the R6 `CodeableReference` structure. In the reverse direction, an R6 `Substance.code.reference` to `SubstanceDefinition` has no native slot in R4 `Substance.code` unless the referenced definition is resolved to a code or carried in an extension.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Substance identity is clinically and operationally important; an incorrect transform from reference to coding or vice versa can change which material a system believes is being handled.

justification.inferredGoal: Allow a `Substance` instance to identify its substance by either terminology or a richer R6 `SubstanceDefinition` resource.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep `Substance.code` as `CodeableConcept` and add a separate optional `SubstanceDefinition` reference.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The inferred goal is reasonable: R6 `CodeableReference` lets the required substance identity be either a terminology concept or an exact `SubstanceDefinition` reference in one semantic slot. A less-breaking separate-reference design is plausible, but it would either require redundant coding when the reference is authoritative or add rules for reconciling two identity fields. Those are material interoperability and implementation tradeoffs, so the breaking design is probably justified rather than clearly avoidable.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best less-breaking base design would have retained `Substance.code` as the mandatory R4 `CodeableConcept` and added an optional `Substance.definition` or `Substance.codeReference` to `SubstanceDefinition`. That would keep R4 instances valid and still permit richer linkage. It is only a partial alternative because it does not cleanly support a reference-only identity without either duplicating a code or weakening the old required concept, and it would require explicit precedence and consistency rules between concept and reference.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves R4 concept-shaped instances, but creates duplicate identity slots, consistency/precedence rules, and weaker support for reference-only identity.

evidence.detail: R6 declares `Substance.code` type `CodeableReference` with target profile `SubstanceDefinition` and cardinality 1..1.
R6 `CodeableReference` represents either a `concept` (`CodeableConcept`) or a `reference` (`Reference`).

examples.examplesMd: The R4 example illustrates the old direct `CodeableConcept` shape. The migration example wraps the same concept under `code.concept`; if the R6 instance uses `code.reference`, reverse migration needs a resolvable code or an extension.

findings.narrativeMd: `Substance.code` kept its name and cardinality but changed from a direct `CodeableConcept` to `CodeableReference`. This is easy to miss because the path is unchanged, yet generated classes, JSON serializers, FHIRPath expressions, and validators must use a different structure. Since `code` is mandatory, every conformant `Substance` instance must be migrated.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4 instance containing `Substance.code.coding` directly is old-valid/new-invalid under the R6 StructureDefinition. R6 instances that use `Substance.code.reference` are not cleanly representable in R4 without dereferencing to a `CodeableConcept` or preserving the reference in an extension. Runtime failures are likely in strict parsers and enum/search code that expected `Substance.code` to be a `CodeableConcept`.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Update models and transforms so R4 `Substance.code` maps to R6 `Substance.code.concept`. For R6-to-R4, decide whether `code.reference` can be resolved to a code from the referenced `SubstanceDefinition`; if not, use a cross-version extension or manual review. Test both concept-only and reference-only R6 examples.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The change is probably motivated by the richer R6 substance-definition model, but it is not wire-compatible. A separate optional reference element would have preserved R4 instances while adding R6 capability; the tradeoff would be a more redundant model and a need to define precedence between concept and reference.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 `Substance.code` is a mandatory `CodeableConcept`; R6 keeps the same path and cardinality but changes the wire shape to `CodeableReference`, with the old concept form now under `code.concept` and a new possible reference to `SubstanceDefinition`. An R4 Substance with `code.coding` directly under `code` needs transformation before R6 validation or generated-model deserialization, and an R6 reference-only code cannot be represented in R4 without resolving the referenced definition or carrying extra data. The break is real and central to Substance identity, but the R6 goal of allowing either terminology identity or a definitional resource in one semantic slot is coherent. Separate legacy and reference fields would preserve more R4 payloads but introduce duplicate identity slots and precedence rules.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition: `Substance.code` is 1..1 `CodeableConcept` with example binding to `ValueSet/substance-code`.
R6 StructureDefinition: `Substance.code` is 1..1 `CodeableReference` targeting `SubstanceDefinition` with the same example binding.
R6 adds `SearchParameter/Substance-code-reference` for `Substance.code.reference` while token code search moves to `Substance.code.concept`.
freshReview.fmmEffect: R4 Substance is FMM 2/trial-use, so maturity is neutral rather than a strong stability guarantee; the central required path and hard wire-shape change still make this a real migration burden.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid and runtime/API/codegen: R4 concept-shaped JSON at `Substance.code` is not the R6 CodeableReference child shape, and generated models/search expressions change; R6 reference-only values also create R6-to-R4 loss unless resolved.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A less-breaking base design could have kept `code` as `CodeableConcept` and added an optional `definition` or `codeReference`. That would preserve R4 instances but would split one identity concept across two fields, require consistency and precedence rules, and make reference-only identity awkward.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree with the existing high-impact assessment and its partial less-breaking alternative judgment; the break is substantial, but the alternative has material design tradeoffs.

findings.title: Repeatable Substance.instance backbone was removed and only partly flattened

oldState.summary: `Substance.instance` was a repeatable backbone for package/container instances.

semanticText.short: If this describes a specific package/container of the substance
semanticText.definition: Substance may be used to describe a kind of substance, or a specific package/container of the substance: an instance.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 could carry zero or more package/container instances, each with its own optional `identifier`, `expiry`, and `quantity`.

newState.summary: `Substance.instance` is absent; R6 has top-level optional `expiry` and `quantity`, and `identifier` text now mentions package/container identifiers.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 removes the nested repeatable container and exposes only one top-level `expiry` and one top-level `quantity`. There is no remaining local element that preserves multiple per-container groups.

facts.note: The replacement is partial because the repeatable grouping by package/container is not preserved.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: `Substance.instance.expiry` and `Substance.instance.quantity` have the same short/definition text as new top-level `Substance.expiry` and `Substance.quantity`, while `Substance.instance.identifier` appears folded into the broader `Substance.identifier` meaning.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Any R4 instance containing `Substance.instance` uses an element that is absent from R6 and will be rejected by strict R6 validation. Transforming a single R4 instance is plausible, but multiple R4 instances cannot be represented as separate grouped packages in R6 `Substance` without loss or extensions.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Package/container identifiers, quantities, and expiry dates are operationally important for inventory, dispensing, and traceability. Losing grouping can associate the wrong lot-like identifier with the wrong quantity or expiry date.

justification.inferredGoal: Simplify `Substance` by representing a single material/package view directly on the resource rather than through a repeatable nested backbone.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain deprecated `Substance.instance` 0..* while adding top-level `expiry`, `quantity`, and package-aware identifier guidance.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Flattening package/container details onto `Substance` is a reasonable R6 simplification goal, especially for the single-package case. Keeping the old repeatable backbone would have reduced validation breakage, but it would also preserve a competing grouped representation for the same facts and keep allowing multiple package instances inside one resource when R6 appears to model only one top-level package view. Because those tradeoffs are material, the less-breaking path is partial and the removal is probably justified, though not definitively proven by the local files alone.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design could have kept `Substance.instance` as deprecated 0..* and introduced top-level `expiry` and `quantity` as the preferred R6 representation. This would preserve all R4 instances, including multi-instance records, but would force implementations to handle conflicts between `instance.expiry` and `expiry`, `instance.quantity` and `quantity`, and old grouped package identifiers versus top-level identifiers. The duplicate same-resource representations could become permanent unless the specification supplied strong invariants, search rules, and migration policy.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Would preserve old package groups, but duplicates package facts, complicates validation/search consistency, and lets deprecated multi-instance representations persist indefinitely.

evidence.quote: Substance may be used to describe a kind of substance, or a specific package/container of the substance: an instance.

evidence.detail: R4 nested package/container details include identifier, expiry, and quantity.
R6 has no `Substance.instance` element, but does add top-level `Substance.expiry` and `Substance.quantity`.

examples.examplesMd: The migration example is lossless only for a single R4 `instance`. If the R4 resource has multiple `instance` repetitions, R6 `Substance` has no native way to retain each identifier/expiry/quantity grouping.

findings.narrativeMd: R4 allowed a `Substance` resource to describe multiple package/container instances inside `Substance.instance`. R6 removes that backbone and only carries top-level `expiry` and `quantity`, plus a broadened `identifier`. This is a hard validation break for old data and a model break for systems that handled lots, containers, or packages as repeated child objects.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4 resource with any `instance` repetition is old-valid/new-invalid because `Substance.instance` is not in the R6 StructureDefinition. A one-instance resource can often be transformed, but the transform is not generally reversible: R6 lacks the old grouping, and R4-to-R6 migration of multiple instances requires splitting resources, extensions, or a related inventory/product model.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Identify all R4 `Substance.instance` use. For one repetition, map `instance.identifier` to `identifier`, `instance.expiry` to `expiry`, and `instance.quantity` to `quantity`, while also applying the `code` `CodeableReference` transform. For multiple repetitions, define policy: split into multiple R6 resources, preserve repetitions in extensions, or migrate to a domain-specific inventory/package artifact. Test multiple-instance records explicitly.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The flattening may simplify the base resource but discards a repeatable local structure. The least disruptive alternative would have been to keep the backbone as deprecated and add top-level fields; this would have allowed old instances to validate while implementers gradually adopted the flatter model.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: The StructureDefinitions prove removal and top-level additions, but they do not prove the intended official handling of multiple package/container instances.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 allowed repeatable `Substance.instance` groups for package/container-specific identifier, expiry, and quantity. R6 removes the backbone and exposes only single top-level `expiry` and `quantity`, while package/container identifiers appear to be folded into the repeated top-level `identifier`. A single R4 instance can often be mechanically flattened, but repeatable R4 package groups lose grouping and may require splitting one Substance into multiple resources or using extensions. That is more than a simple cleanup because package labels, amounts, and expiry are operational traceability facts.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition: `Substance.instance` is 0..* BackboneElement with `identifier`, `expiry`, and `quantity` children.
R6 StructureDefinition: no `Substance.instance`; `Substance.expiry` and `Substance.quantity` are top-level 0..1 elements.

R4 search expressions for `expiry` and `quantity` point to `Substance.instance.expiry` and `Substance.instance.quantity`; R6 expressions point to top-level `Substance.expiry` and `Substance.quantity`.
R4 has a separate `container-identifier` search on `Substance.instance.identifier`; R6 has no analogous separate container search in the local package.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 2/trial-use does not by itself demand preserving the old backbone, but it also does not soften a lossy, operationally relevant migration enough to dismiss it.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid and R6-to-R4 loss: any R4 payload using `Substance.instance` is invalid as R6, and multiple package/container groups cannot be faithfully represented by the single top-level R6 fields without splitting resources or adding non-base data.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Retaining `Substance.instance` as deprecated while adding preferred top-level fields would preserve R4 instances and permit staged migration. The tradeoff is duplicate representations and conflict rules between old grouped data and new flattened data, but that seems a plausible transitional base design given the loss of repeatable package grouping.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree with the existing high-impact assessment, but disagree that the partial alternative is enough to call the removal probably justified without renewed review; the lossy multi-instance case is the concern.

findings.title: Substance.ingredient backbone was removed from the resource

semanticText.definition: A substance can be composed of other substances.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 could represent composition directly inside `Substance`, including an optional concentration ratio and a mandatory ingredient substance represented as a code or reference to another `Substance`.

newState.summary: No `Substance.ingredient` element exists in the R6 `Substance` resource.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 removes the local composition backbone. Related R6 artifacts such as `Ingredient` and `SubstanceDefinition.relationship` may carry some substance-composition concepts, but there is no direct in-resource replacement.

facts.note: These are related R6 models, not direct local replacements.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The R4 `Substance.ingredient` element and children are absent from the R6 `Substance` differential and snapshot.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Any R4 instance carrying `Substance.ingredient` will be invalid as an R6 `Substance`. The runtime risk is high for generated models or business logic that expected composition to be available inline. R6-to-R4 representability is low for this specific resource because R6 `Substance` has no equivalent local ingredient content to map back.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Composition and concentration can be clinically and regulatory significant. Dropping or misplacing this data can affect downstream safety, labeling, or analytics.

justification.inferredGoal: Move composition and product-ingredient detail out of the lightweight `Substance` resource into more specialized R6 substance/product artifacts.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain deprecated `Substance.ingredient` 0..* with guidance to use R6 `Ingredient` or `SubstanceDefinition` for new content.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Moving composition and ingredient detail out of lightweight `Substance` into more specialized R6 artifacts is a reasonable model goal. Retaining the old inline backbone would avoid immediate validation failures, but it would also perpetuate two places for clinically and regulatory significant composition facts and make it harder for receivers to know which representation is authoritative. That makes the alternative only partial and supports a probably justified verdict, with residual uncertainty because the local package does not provide an official migration map.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best less-breaking base design would keep `Substance.ingredient` as a deprecated optional backbone while making `Ingredient` or `SubstanceDefinition.relationship` the preferred target for richer R6 data. This would preserve R4 instances, but it would not be a clean long-term design: inline ingredient quantities and external ingredient/relationship resources could diverge, validators would need conflict rules, and implementers would carry the deprecated representation indefinitely.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves inline R4 composition, but creates overlapping sources of truth with dedicated R6 ingredient/substance-definition models and a safety-relevant reconciliation burden.

evidence.quote: A substance can be composed of other substances.

evidence.detail: R4 ingredient requires `substance[x]` 1..1 with type `CodeableConcept` or `Reference(Substance)`.
R6 `Substance` contains no `ingredient` element or ingredient child elements.
R6 contains related specialized structures that may be migration targets for some, but not necessarily all, R4 ingredient uses.

examples.examplesMd: The example shows an R4 inline ingredient. R6 migration cannot be shown as a single direct `Substance` fragment because the element was removed; target selection requires domain-specific mapping.

findings.narrativeMd: `Substance.ingredient` was a local R4 place to express composition. R6 removes it entirely from `Substance`, so old instances with inline ingredients fail validation and applications lose a familiar in-resource traversal path for concentration and component substance.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: This is an old-valid/new-invalid change: `Substance.ingredient`, `Substance.ingredient.quantity`, and `Substance.ingredient.substance[x]` have no R6 `Substance` paths. R6-to-R4 representability is not the main issue for `Substance` itself because R6 does not carry that local content; the issue is preserving R4 data somewhere else.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Inventory R4 data that uses `Substance.ingredient`. For each use, decide whether it represents a product ingredient, a substance-definition relationship, a concentration relationship, or local descriptive data. Map to `Ingredient`, `SubstanceDefinition.relationship`, an extension, or manual review as appropriate. Do not silently drop ingredient quantities.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A dedicated model split is understandable, but removal from the base resource is breaking. Keeping the old element as deprecated while adding clearer target artifacts would have allowed R4 instances to remain valid and would have given implementers a gradual migration path.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Official migration guidance would materially improve confidence about whether `Ingredient` or `SubstanceDefinition.relationship` is the preferred target for each R4 pattern.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 `Substance.ingredient` was an optional repeatable inline composition backbone with an optional concentration ratio and a required ingredient substance by code or Substance reference. R6 removes this inline content from `Substance`; related composition information appears to move to more specialized R6 artifacts such as `Ingredient` and `SubstanceDefinition.relationship`. Existing R4 instances with inline ingredients will fail R6 structural validation and generated code that expected inline composition must migrate. The break is meaningful, but moving composition and ingredient strength into dedicated structures is a reasonable model direction, and retaining the old inline backbone would create competing sources of truth for safety-relevant composition data.
keyEvidence: R6 Substance snapshot has no `Substance.ingredient` element.
R6 Ingredient has `Ingredient.substance.code` as a required `CodeableReference`; R6 SubstanceDefinition has repeatable `relationship` with a related substance and amount fields.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 2/trial-use is neutral: it lowers the expectation compared with mature/normative content, but composition can still be clinically or regulatory significant where used.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid and runtime/API/codegen: R4 inline ingredient content is not accepted on R6 Substance, and business logic or SDK properties for inline composition disappear. Reverse loss is limited for this path because R6 Substance has no replacement inline ingredient field.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: R6 could have kept `Substance.ingredient` as a deprecated optional backbone while recommending `Ingredient` or `SubstanceDefinition.relationship` for new content. That would preserve R4 instances, but it would maintain overlapping composition models and require reconciliation rules when inline and dedicated-resource facts disagree.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree with the existing high-impact and partial-alternative assessment; the break is real, but the cleaner R6 composition model makes the less-breaking option costly.

findings.title: Substance.description primitive type changed from string to markdown

semanticText.short: Textual description of the substance, comments
semanticText.definition: A description of the substance - its appearance, handling requirements, and other usage notes.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 treated the description as plain string content.

semanticText.short: Textual description of the substance, comments
semanticText.definition: A description of the substance - its appearance, handling requirements, and other usage notes.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 keeps the same element path and JSON primitive wire type, but the declared FHIR primitive is now `markdown`, allowing GFM-style markup.

facts.note: The wire primitive remains JSON string, but generated and schema-level types differ.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The same element id/path remains present with unchanged cardinality and semantic definition; only the primitive type changed.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Most R4 description values are still representable as R6 markdown because both serialize as JSON strings. The practical risk is in code generation, schema validation, rendering, escaping/sanitization, and UI assumptions about whether markdown is processed.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: The field is descriptive, but rendering markdown without an established sanitization policy can create display or content interpretation issues.

justification.inferredGoal: Permit formatted narrative notes about substance appearance, handling, or usage.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: No less-breaking base alternative is needed for R4 instance validity; ordinary R4 string values remain JSON strings and markdown specializes string.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: This is not a hard R4-to-R6 instance-design break: `markdown` is still serialized as a string primitive and is a specialization of `string`, so ordinary R4 `description` values remain representable. The main risks are generated type churn, UI rendering, escaping, and sanitization. The goal of allowing formatted descriptive notes is reasonable, and the compatibility impact is modest, so the change is probably justified and `backwardCompatibleAlternativeAvailable` is not applicable.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: Keeping `description` as `string`, or adding a markdown extension, would reduce model churn for generated APIs but is not a needed base-design alternative to preserve R4-valid instances. Those options would make formatted descriptions less discoverable and less consistently handled by R6 systems.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Retaining `string` would avoid generated-type and rendering review, but would not provide standard markdown semantics.

evidence.detail: R6 markdown is a string primitive intended for optional GFM processing.

examples.examplesMd: Plain text can usually be carried forward unchanged. Systems should test markdown metacharacters and rendering/sanitization behavior separately.

findings.narrativeMd: `Substance.description` changes from `string` to `markdown`. This is not usually a data-validation break at the JSON primitive level, but it is a real type-domain and semantic change for generated classes, schema-aware validators, display components, and sanitization policies.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: A normal R4 string value should generally remain valid as an R6 markdown string, so this is not counted as hard instance-breaking. However, strict generated APIs may expose a different primitive type, and R6 markdown content may be rendered or interpreted differently when converted back to R4 systems that treat the field as plain text.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Map the string value directly, but update code generation, serializers, UI rendering, and security review to treat the R6 field as markdown. Include test cases with plain text, markdown punctuation, line breaks, and any application-specific sanitization rules.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The change could have been avoided by retaining `string`, but the compatibility cost is modest compared with the benefit of standard markdown semantics. A separate extension would reduce generated-type churn but would make formatted descriptions less interoperable.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 `Substance.description` was an optional `string`; R6 changes it to optional `markdown` with the same cardinality and JSON primitive representation. Ordinary R4 plain-text descriptions remain representable as R6 markdown. Some generated APIs, renderers, or sanitization policies may need to notice the primitive type name, but this is not a base instance-compatibility problem and the field is descriptive rather than a core computable safety field.
keyEvidence: R6 StructureDefinition: `Substance.description` is 0..1 `markdown` with the same definition text.
FHIR primitive markdown is still serialized as a string value; no cardinality or binding change is involved.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 2/trial-use is neutral; because there is no old-valid/new-invalid change for normal string values, maturity does not create a reason to revisit the design.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: runtime/API/codegen only at most: generated primitive wrappers or rendering policy may change, but the wire representation remains a JSON string and plain text remains valid markdown.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Keeping `string` would avoid minor type-name churn, but no less-breaking base design is needed to preserve R4 instances; using markdown gives a standard way to express formatted descriptive text.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree with the existing runtime-risk observation, but disagree with treating it as a meaningful medium compatibility concern; it is not a substantive base break.

findings.title: Substance.identifier semantics broadened to include package/container identifiers

oldState.summary: `Substance.identifier` identified the kind of substance and was explicitly contrasted with `Substance.instance.identifier`.

semanticText.comment: This identifier is associated with the kind of substance in contrast to the  Substance.instance.identifier which is associated with the package/container.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 separated identifiers for the substance kind from identifiers on specific packages/containers.

newState.summary: `Substance.identifier` now explicitly may be associated with the package/container of the substance instance.

semanticText.definition: Unique identifier for the substance, often an identifier associated with the package/container of the substance instance (usually a label affixed directly).

newState.narrativeMd: R6 keeps the same cardinality and type but broadens the element's meaning after removing the separate `instance.identifier` path.

facts.newValue: Unique identifier for the substance, often an identifier associated with the package/container of the substance instance (usually a label affixed directly).

facts.oldValue: This identifier is associated with the kind of substance in contrast to the Substance.instance.identifier which is associated with the package/container.
facts.note: The old separation is no longer present because `Substance.instance.identifier` was removed.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The element id/path, type, and cardinality are unchanged; the material change is in definition/comment semantics.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Validation does not change, but business semantics do. R4 systems could rely on `Substance.identifier` for substance-kind identifiers and `Substance.instance.identifier` for package/container labels. R6 collapses those meanings into one repeating identifier field unless profiles or identifier types restore the distinction.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Confusing a substance identity with a package/container or lot label can affect inventory, traceability, and decision support.

justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep `Substance.identifier` scoped to substance identity and add a distinct `containerIdentifier`, or retain deprecated `instance.identifier`, for package labels.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Preserving package/container labels after removing `Substance.instance.identifier` is a reasonable goal, but broadening the meaning of the existing `Substance.identifier` creates avoidable semantic ambiguity. A distinct identifier slot would preserve the R4 interpretation for existing `Substance.identifier` values while still supporting package labels with low to moderate long-term cost. Because that less-breaking base design appears to meet the goal without relying on conversion tooling or profiles alone, this semantic break was probably avoidable.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best alternative would be a separate optional `Substance.containerIdentifier` 0..* or a retained deprecated `Substance.instance.identifier` path for package/container labels. Either keeps existing R4 substance-kind identifiers valid with their prior meaning and gives R6 systems a clear place for package labels. The tradeoff is one more element and explicit mapping/search guidance, but that is less costly than overloading a single repeating identifier field and requiring receivers to infer scope from `Identifier.type` conventions.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Adds an element and migration guidance, but avoids semantic collision between material identifiers and package/container identifiers.

evidence.detail: R4 definition identifies the substance and the comment contrasts it with package/container identifiers on `Substance.instance.identifier`.
R6 definition says the identifier is often associated with the package/container of the substance instance.
R6 no longer contains `Substance.instance.identifier` as a separate path.

examples.examplesMd: The example uses `Identifier.type.text` to preserve identifier scope. Actual systems should use stable coding systems or profiles where possible.

findings.narrativeMd: The path `Substance.identifier` did not change structurally, but its meaning did. R4 distinguished identifiers for the substance kind from package/container identifiers. R6 says `identifier` is often a package/container identifier, which means migrations must preserve identifier scope explicitly or risk conflating different business identifiers.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: This is not a hard validation break because the type and cardinality remain `Identifier` 0..*. The break is semantic and runtime-oriented: queries, deduplication, inventory matching, and generated helper methods that assumed a kind-level identifier may behave differently after migration.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: When moving R4 `instance.identifier` values into R6 `identifier`, tag them with `Identifier.type`, system conventions, profile slices, or extensions so consumers can tell package/container labels from substance-kind identifiers. Add tests for search, deduplication, and display logic that uses identifiers.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The semantic broadening was probably an attempt to avoid losing package labels after removing `Substance.instance`, but a dedicated element or retained deprecated child would have been clearer and more backward-compatible.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: This finding is intentionally separate from the `Substance.instance` removal because code can pass validation while still misinterpreting identifiers.

freshReview.narrativeMd: The `Substance.identifier` wire shape did not change, but its R6 meaning broadened. In R4, the top-level identifier was for the substance kind and the comment explicitly contrasted it with `Substance.instance.identifier` for package/container labels. In R6, after removal of `instance.identifier`, the same top-level repeated identifier is described as often being associated with the package/container. That preserves structural validity but creates a semantic collision for search, matching, traceability, and R6-to-R4 mapping: a receiver cannot reliably tell whether an identifier denotes the material or a particular package unless profiles or identifier typing conventions fill the gap.
keyEvidence: R4 `Substance.identifier` definition: unique identifier for the substance; comment contrasts it with `Substance.instance.identifier` for package/container.
R6 `Substance.identifier` definition: unique identifier for the substance, often associated with the package/container of the substance instance.
R4 had separate `SearchParameter/Substance-container-identifier` on `Substance.instance.identifier`; R6 local package has only `Substance.identifier` for `Substance.identifier`.
R6 removes `Substance.instance.identifier` as a distinct path.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 2/trial-use is neutral, but the affected meaning is operationally important for package traceability and matching, so the semantic break should not be dismissed as low maturity experimentation.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: semantic/documentation and R6-to-R4 loss: validation does not fail, but the same field now mixes material identifiers and package/container identifiers, making old assumptions and reverse mapping ambiguous.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A distinct optional `containerIdentifier` element, or a deprecated retained `instance.identifier`, would preserve the R4 top-level identifier meaning while still supporting package labels. The tradeoff is an extra element and mapping/search guidance, which appears modest compared with overloading one identifier field.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree with the existing avoidable-break assessment and its yes less-breaking alternative judgment.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: The canonical URL, id, name, kind, type, baseDefinition, derivation, and abstract flag are unchanged. R6 changes lifecycle metadata such as status/publisher/date, but not identity.

For local element paths that remain in both versions (`identifier`, `status`, `category`, `code`, `description`), cardinalities are unchanged. Cardinality impact from removed/added paths is covered in findings.

`Substance.status` remains required and the underlying local code system concepts are unchanged (`active`, `inactive`, `entered-in-error`). `Substance.category` retains the same ValueSet compose include, but the R6 package did not include the external category CodeSystem content. The `substance-code` example ValueSet changed and is listed as a notable non-breaking change.
No local `Substance` invariant was added, removed, or changed in the differential. Snapshot constraint changes observed on root/extension paths are inherited base-artifact changes and out of scope.
The local modifier status of `Substance.status` remains true. No local element gains or loses modifier status.
Local summary flags for retained local elements remain materially consistent. Inherited `modifierExtension` summary-flag differences are excluded as base-artifact scope.
No local slicing was identified on R4 or R6 `Substance` elements.
No local fixed value, pattern, or default value was identified for `Substance` in either version.
No local maxLength, regex, minValue, or maxValue changes were identified on `Substance` elements apart from primitive datatype behavior handled by the `description` finding.

The material reference-target change is covered by the `Substance.code` `CodeableReference(SubstanceDefinition)` finding and the removal of `ingredient.substance[x]`. No other retained local `Substance` reference target changed.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: StructureDefinition lifecycle metadata changed from draft to active
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The StructureDefinition `status` changed from `draft` in R4 to `active` in R6, and publisher/workgroup metadata changed. This affects governance interpretation but not instance validity or wire representation.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Organizations that gate adoption on maturity/status may treat the R6 artifact differently.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: substance-status ValueSet version changed but required codes are unchanged
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: `Substance.status` remains required-bound to `ValueSet/substance-status`, and the local complete CodeSystem concepts remain `active`, `inactive`, and `entered-in-error` with the same definitions.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Validators that pin value-set versions should update from `|4.0.1` to `|6.0.0-ballot4`, but no code remapping was identified.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: substance-code example ValueSet compose narrowed from two SNOMED filters to one
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The binding strength on `Substance.code` is `example`, so the ValueSet compose change does not make formerly valid codes invalid by itself.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: R4 included SNOMED filters for concepts 105590001 and 373873005; R6 includes only 105590001. Implementations that used the example ValueSet as a pick-list or policy constraint should review product/substance code coverage.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 adds top-level expiry and quantity
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: Adding optional top-level elements is not by itself R4-to-R6 instance-breaking. The breaking aspect is that the old repeatable `Substance.instance` backbone was removed, which is covered in a finding.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: These elements are likely the direct targets for a single R4 `instance.expiry` and `instance.quantity`, but they do not preserve multiple per-container groups.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 explicitly records mustSupport false on local elements
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: R4 generally omits `mustSupport` in the base StructureDefinition, while R6 explicitly records false on many elements. Omitted and false are not materially different for base instance validation.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Code generators that distinguish absent from false should normalize this as no support requirement.

followUpDependencies.reasonMd: `Substance.code` can now reference `SubstanceDefinition`; migration quality depends on how R6 substance definitions carry codes, names, relationships, and identifiers.
Some R4 `Substance.ingredient` content may need to move to R6 `Ingredient`, but the correct mapping depends on product context and required `Ingredient` fields.
The example-bound ValueSet compose changed from two SNOMED filters to one. A terminology expansion would quantify practical code-list impact for implementations that used it as a pick-list.
Inherited snapshot changes were visible in `Substance` but intentionally excluded from local findings per scope rules.

analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Review official R6 ballot narrative pages, change notes, or Jira tickets for the Substance remodel.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: No ConceptMap or official migration transform was available for `Substance` to `SubstanceDefinition`, `Ingredient`, or other R6 artifacts.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Use official cross-version maps or implementation-guide migration rules, if available.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: The SNOMED CT filters in `ValueSet/substance-code` were compared at the compose level only; no terminology server expansion was performed.
